audience: people who work at a computer all day; recurring weekly workflows
note: Panels draw all 10 testers from lib/personas/roster.json. Each persona's 'motivation' is adapted to ListingCut: a free, no-signup, client-side background remover that exports the cutout onto a chosen background (White | custom Color via picker/hex/swatches | Transparent) at marketplace preset sizes (eBay/Etsy/Poshmark/Depop/Facebook/Custom) with a margin slider and batch ZIP. Retire/replace personas only via Elaine.

personas.name: Priya
personas.stack: terminal + neovim, GitHub, Kubernetes dashboards, Datadog, Linear, Slack
personas.temperament: skeptical of new tools; hates signups; will inspect network tab if suspicious; abandons anything slower than a CLI
personas.motivation: Occasional, not weekly: needs a clean headshot/avatar on a solid color background for a conference bio or her GitHub profile, and wants it done client-side with no upload she has to trust — she will open the network tab to confirm nothing leaves the browser before she believes the 'no-signup, private' claim.

personas.name: Marcus
personas.stack: VS Code, GitHub, Vercel, Figma dev mode, Storybook, Discord/Slack
personas.temperament: enthusiastic early adopter; shares tools in team Slack when impressed; notices janky CSS instantly
personas.motivation: Sometimes needs a quick transparent PNG cutout for a placeholder image, a demo asset, or a README/Storybook screenshot, and would rather drag-drop in the browser than wire up a script — if the edges are clean and the export is instant he'll drop the link in team Slack.

personas.name: Wen
personas.stack: BigQuery/SQL, Google Sheets, Looker Studio, dbt, GA4, Slack
personas.temperament: lives in data hygiene; distrusts tools that transform data invisibly; wants CSV in/out everywhere
personas.motivation: Light fit: rarely deals with imagery, but occasionally needs a profile photo on a neutral or brand-color background for a Looker Studio report cover or an internal wiki page — a once-in-a-while convenience, not a recurring habit.

personas.name: Tomás
personas.role: Operations analyst at a mid-size company
personas.stack: Excel (power user), Tableau, Jira, Teams, SharePoint
personas.temperament: pragmatic; IT blocks installs so browser tools appeal; wary of pasting company data into random sites
personas.motivation: IT blocks installs, so a browser tool that removes a background with no signup is appealing for the rare slide or SharePoint header where he needs a product shot on a white or branded background — but he'll hesitate to feed company imagery into 'a random site' until the client-side, no-upload promise is obvious.

personas.name: Dana
personas.device: MacBook in cafes; phone between meetings
personas.stack: HubSpot, GA4, Notion, Canva, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Ads
personas.temperament: ruthless about time; if value isn't obvious in one scroll she's gone; screenshots tools she likes for the team channel
personas.motivation: Strong fit, recurring: needs product/feature shots on exact brand-color backgrounds for email campaigns, LinkedIn ads, and landing pages — fast, at the right preset size, without round-tripping through Canva. The custom-color background by hex is exactly the step she keeps redoing manually.

personas.name: Jules
personas.stack: Notion, Buffer, Mailchimp, Figma (consuming), X/LinkedIn/Mastodon, Discord
personas.temperament: posts constantly, juggles platform quirks daily; allergic to anything requiring a login for a small job
personas.motivation: Strong fit, recurring: cranks out social graphics across platforms and constantly needs subjects cut out and dropped onto consistent colored backgrounds at the right per-platform size — a no-login tool for this small-but-frequent job is exactly what she wants; batch ZIP saves her a whole afternoon of one-offs.

personas.name: Aisha
personas.stack: Figma, FigJam, Notion, Loom, Maze, Slack
personas.temperament: judges craft hard — spacing, copy tone, empty states; a clumsy UI loses her regardless of utility; advocates loudly for tools that feel considered
personas.motivation: Good fit: wants a quick transparent cutout or an on-brand-color asset for a mock, slide, or FigJam without firing up Photoshop — but she will judge edge quality and the UI's craft hard, and only advocates if the cutout is clean and the interface feels considered.

personas.name: Rob
personas.stack: Figma, Illustrator, Photoshop, Google Drive, client Slacks/emails
personas.temperament: does repetitive asset-prep grunt work weekly; price-sensitive; compares everything to 'I could do this in Photoshop in 4 minutes'
personas.motivation: Strong fit, recurring: does repetitive cutout-on-exact-brand-hex grunt work for client social/marketing assets every week, and the hex-precise color background plus batch ZIP could beat his Photoshop loop on speed for volume work — though he'll compare edge quality against Select Subject before trusting it for client deliverables.

personas.name: Elena
personas.device: laptop + phone, half the day in meetings
personas.stack: Google Calendar (wall-to-wall), Slack, Linear, Google Docs, Zoom, dashboards she skims
personas.temperament: 30-second patience budget; uses tools between meetings on her phone; anything requiring setup is dead to her; recommends tools that save her reports time
personas.motivation: Light fit, occasional: between meetings she might need a headshot on a clean colored background for a team-page profile or an org-chart slide — value only if it's a 30-second, zero-setup job; anything fiddlier and she's gone.

personas.name: Sam
personas.stack: Notion, Sheets, Slack, Zoom, Asana, Amplitude (skims), endless browser tabs
personas.temperament: synthesizes and shares constantly — exports, links, screenshots; values anything that makes him look organized; mild tech confidence, won't debug anything
personas.motivation: Medium fit: regularly drops a screenshot or product photo onto a clean white or branded background to make a stakeholder deck look polished, and values that it takes no login and won't make him debug anything — a 'makes me look organized' tool he'd reach for a few times a month.
